newsitem.title: USA: Female Health sees higher 1st half revenues.
newsitem.headline: Female Health sees higher 1st half revenues.

text.p: Female Health Co said it expects revenues for the first half of fiscal 1997 to increase 43 percent from the prior-year period.
The company also said, as noted previously, it expects to record a net loss until it reaches a break-even level of volume.
Last month, Female Health reported a loss for the first quarter ended December 31 of $0.22 a share on revenues of $605,818.
For the first six months of fiscal 1996, Female Health's revenues were $731,000.

Female Health, which owns certain worldwide rights to the female condom, said it also is in discussions with potential partners for Europe and the United States to capitalize on market potential for its product.
Female Health said it recently received European Union approval for the female condom.

The company currently has partners in certain key countries including Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, the Netherlands and Canada. It is also holding discussions with potential partners in India, China, Brazil, Mexico, Russia and Australia/New Zealand.
Female Health said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved an extension of the shelf life of the female condom to 60 months from 36 months.
